deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the survey opening of Grothendieck's 1967 talk on crystals. It motivates why an 'integral' cohomology is needed in characteristic p.

Setting: X is a variety over an algebraically closed field k, and H^i(X,Z_ℓ) = lim H^i(X_et, Z/ℓ^ν) for ℓ ≠ char k.

Over C, the comparison theorem gives H^i(X,Z_ℓ) ≅ H^i(X^an,Z) ⊗ Z_ℓ. This page draws the consequences:
(1) Knowing all H^i(X,Z_ℓ) is equivalent to knowing H^i(X^an,Z), prime by prime. For a fixed ℓ, H^i(X,Z_ℓ) determines and is determined by two things: the Betti number b_i(X) = rank H^i(X^an,Z), which is the Z_ℓ-rank of H^i(X,Z_ℓ); and the ℓ-primary part of the torsion subgroup of H^i(X^an,Z). This uses that H^i(X^an,Z) is finitely generated, so its ℓ-adic completion is that tensor product.
(2) Hence, by transcendental means, in characteristic 0:
- the H^i(X,Z_ℓ) are finitely generated;
- their ranks b_i are independent of ℓ;
- for fixed X, only finitely many ℓ give torsion in H^i(X,Z_ℓ).
For an arbitrary algebraically closed k of characteristic 0 this is implicitly reduced to C, by invariance of étale cohomology under extension of algebraically closed fields plus a Lefschetz-principle descent.
(3) For an endomorphism f of X, the characteristic polynomials of f* on H^i(X,Z_ℓ) have integer coefficients independent of ℓ. They come from the characteristic polynomial of f* on the lattice H^i(X^an,Z)/torsion.

The next page contrasts this with characteristic p > 0, where there is no transcendental integral cohomology:
- finiteness of H^i(X,Z_ℓ) was then known only for X proper or dim X ≤ 2;
- ℓ-independence of b_2, and integrality/ℓ-independence of characteristic polynomials, were open, being consequences of the Weil conjectures.

Role of the page: it motivates the search for a p-adic/crystalline 'integral' theory. It is purely expository background.
errors: One implicit step: the comparison theorem applies only over C. Extending the char-0 conclusions to an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 requires a specialization/Lefschetz-principle argument (invariance of étale cohomology under extension of algebraically closed base field), which is not stated.

ideas.what: Equivalence between knowing all ℓ-adic cohomology groups and knowing integral Betti cohomology (rank plus ℓ-primary torsion), via the comparison theorem
ideas.modern_name: Artin comparison theorem and its consequences
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. XI/XVI; introduction of 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: In char 0: ℓ-independence of Betti numbers, and torsion-freeness of H^i(X,Z_ℓ) for almost all ℓ
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence of Betti numbers; torsion-freeness for almost all ℓ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore via comparison; in char p, Gabber (1983) for torsion-freeness for almost all ℓ, Deligne (Weil I) for Betti numbers of smooth projective varieties
ideas.where_published: Discussed in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969)

ideas.what: Characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms acting on ℓ-adic cohomology have integer coefficients independent of ℓ (char 0, via the integral lattice); open in char p in 1967
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Weil I, 1974) for Frobenius; Katz–Messing (1974) for general endomorphisms of smooth projective varieties

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard expository background for the crystals lecture. It matches the introduction of Grothendieck's published 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'si [?] le corps de base $k$ est de car. [?] ... 0' should read 'si le corps de base k est de car. 0, alors les H^i(X,Z_ℓ) sont de t.f., leurs rangs b_i(X,Z_ℓ) ... sont indépendants de ℓ'. The insertion above the line belongs between 'alors les' and 'pour la variété'.
'si $k$ est un corps de nombres [?]. Si [?] de $X$' is likely 'si f est un endomorphisme de X'. The next page continues 'induit par f'. It is not 'corps de nombres'.
'les polynômes caractéristiques de l'action [?] de' is likely 'de l'endomorphisme de H^i(X,Z_ℓ)'.
Line 1: the crossed-out words are 'entièrement déterminée par', and the insertion above them is 'équivalente à'. The circled word on line 2 is 'tous'.
